source.title: Invitation to H-systems in higher dimensions: known results, new facts, and related open problems

accepted.question_text: Let n >= 3, let B^n be the unit ball in R^n, let N be a compact closed Riemannian manifold isometrically embedded in R^m, and let pi be the nearest-point projection from a tubular neighborhood of N onto N. For the n-Dirichlet energy E_n[v] = (1/n) integral over B^n of |grad v|^n dx, call u in W^{1,n}(B^n,N) weakly n-harmonic when d/dt at t=0 of E_n[pi o (u+t phi)] is zero for every phi in W_0^{1,n}(B^n,R^m) intersect L^infty(B^n,R^m). Must every such weakly n-harmonic map u be continuous on B^n?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we discuss two well-known open problems in the regularity theory for nonlinear, conformally invariant elliptic systems in dimensions n ≥ 3
Definition 2.1. A map u ∈ W 1,p (Ω, N ) is (weakly) p-harmonic if and only if u is a critical point of Ep with respect to variations in the range
Problem 2.2 (p = n). Are all weakly n-harmonic maps u ∈ W 1,n (B n , N ) continuous?

accepted.question_text: Let n > 2, let B^n be the unit ball in R^n, let H: R^{n+1} -> R be bounded and Lipschitz, and let u=(u^1,...,u^{n+1}) be in W^{1,n}(B^n,R^{n+1}). Define J_u as partial_{x_1}u cross ... cross partial_{x_n}u, the vector in R^{n+1} whose coordinates are the n by n minors of Du. If u is a weak solution of the H-system -div(|grad u|^{n-2} grad u) = H(u) J_u, must u be continuous on B^n?

evidence.quote: Set Ju = ∂u/∂x1 × · · · × ∂u/∂xn; for x ∈ B n this is a vector in Rn+1 with coordinates given by the n × n minors of the Jacobi matrix of Du.
Problem 2.4. Let n > 2. Suppose that H : Rn+1 → R is bounded and Lipschitz. Are all weak solutions u ∈ W 1,n (B n , Rn+1 ) of (2.5) continuous?

accepted.question_text: Let u be in W^{1,n}(B^n,R^m) and suppose u satisfies the degenerate n-Laplace system -div(|grad u|^{n-2} grad u) = Omega · |grad u|^{n-2} grad u on B^n. Assume Omega=(Omega^alpha_ij) belongs to L^n(R^{m by m} tensor R^n) and is antisymmetric in the target indices, meaning Omega^alpha_ij = -Omega^alpha_ji for all i and j. Does this antisymmetric-potential structure force u to be continuous?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.5. Let u ∈ W 1,n (B n , Rm ) satisfy a system of the form − div |∇u|n−2 ∇u = Ω · |∇u|n−2 ∇u.
Assume that Ω = (Ωαij ) ∈ L n (Rm×m ⊗ Rn ) is antisymmetric, i.e. Ωαij = −Ωαji for all 1 ≤ i, j ≤ m. Is it true that u is continuous?

accepted.question_text: Let R=(R_1,...,R_n) be the vectorial Riesz transform, let p' be the conjugate exponent to p, and write |Rf| for the Euclidean norm of the Riesz-transform vector. Is it true or false that there is a constant C such that the endpoint Lorentz-space estimate ||f||_{L^{(p,infinity)}}^{p-1} <= C ||sum_{alpha=1}^n R_alpha(|Rf|^{p-2} R_alpha f)||_{L^{(p',infinity)}} holds?
accepted.context_brief: Endpoint Lorentz estimate for Riesz transforms

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2. Let R = (R1 , . . . , Rn ) be the vectorial Riesz transform. Is it true or false that kf kp−1 L(p,∞) ≤ C kΣnα=1 Rα (|Rf |p−2 Rα f )kL(p′ ,∞) ?

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be an open subset of R^n, let H: R^{n+1} -> R be bounded and Lipschitz, and let u=(u^1,...,u^{n+1}) be in W^{1,n}(Omega,R^{n+1}) as a weak solution of the H-system -div(|grad u|^{n-2} grad u) = H(u) J_u. If k of the coordinate functions u^i are bounded, for some k in {1,2,...,n}, must u be continuous?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.4. Let u = (u1 , u2 , . . . , un+1 ) ∈ W 1,n (Ω, Rn+1 ) be a weak solution of the H-system (2.5), where H : Rn+1 → R is bounded and Lipschitz.
Assume that k of the coordinate functions ui are bounded, where k ∈ {1, 2, . . . , n}. Is u continuous?

accepted.question_text: For the p=n harmonic-map system -div(|grad u|^{n-2} grad u) = |grad u|^{n-2} A_u(grad u,grad u) and for the H-system -div(|grad u|^{n-2} grad u) = H(u) J_u, the spaces of weak solutions are closed under weak W^{1,n} convergence, even for corresponding approximate problems with a small perturbation in the dual space (W^{1,n})* added to the right-hand side. Can these weak-closure results be used to construct counterexamples to continuity by taking weak W^{1,n} limits of singular solutions to perturbed versions of those equations?
accepted.context_brief: Counterexamples via weak limits of perturbed solutions

accepted.question_text: Fix H bounded and Lipschitz on R^{n+1}, let u be in W^{1,n}(R^n,R^{n+1}), and set b=H(u), so that b is in W^{1,n}(R^n) intersect L^infty(R^n). Determine the largest subspace V of the Hardy space H^1(R^n) such that the commutator [b,I] maps V to L^{n/(n-1)}(R^n), or to W^{1,1}(R^n) in the variant question; determine whether V contains the n by n minors of Du; determine the largest subspace V such that all commutators [b,R_alpha] with the Riesz transforms map V to L^1(R^n); determine whether du^1 wedge ... wedge du^n has an atomic decomposition into b-atoms, meaning standard atoms additionally orthogonal to b; and determine whether the answers change when u is also assumed to solve an H-system.
accepted.context_brief: Endpoint commutator spaces for H-system data

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. Fix H bounded and Lipschitz on Rn+1 , and u ∈ W 1,n (Rn , Rn+1 ), so that b = H(u) ∈ W 1,n (Rn ) ∩ L∞ (Rn ).
What is the largest subspace V ⊂ H1 (Rn ) such that [b, I] : V → Ln/(n−1) (Rn )? What is the answer if we replace Ln/(n−1) (Rn ) by W 1,1 (Rn )? Does this V contain the n × n minors of Du?
What is the largest subspace V ⊂ H1 (Rn ) such that all commutators [b, Rα ] of the multiplication by b with the Riesz transforms Rα , α = 1, . . . , n, map V → L1 (Rn )?
Does du1 ∧ . . . ∧ dun have an atomic decomposition into b-atoms, i.e. standard atoms that are, in addition, orthogonal to b?
Do the answers to the above questions change if u is not just an element of W 1,n , but also a solution to an H-system?

accepted.question_text: Let B be a ball, let u be in W^{1,n}(B,R^m), and suppose u solves -div(|grad u|^{n-2} grad u) = Omega · |grad u|^{n-2} grad u, where Omega takes values in so(m) tensor R^n and belongs to the Lorentz space L^{(n,p)}. For which p in the interval [1,n] does this assumption imply that u is necessarily continuous?

trace.notes: Normalized the input as the zbMATH resolver URL with identifier 6744543. Direct shell access to zbmath.org was blocked by a Cloudflare challenge or failed with network_or_dns_failure, so the local resolver index was used only to identify the exact same work: title, DOI 10.4171/EMSS/4-1-2, and arXiv URL https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07891. The already-present exact-work PDF at .sisyphus/paper-question-parser/tmp/1606.07891.pdf was used as the readable primary source.

Mapped a 20-page PDF. Section hierarchy: 1 Introduction; 2 Statement of the problems, with subsections 2.1 on n-harmonic maps and 2.2 on H-systems; 3 Partial evidence for regularity, including subsections 3.1-3.4; 4 Approaches based on non-local problems and commutator estimates, including subsections 4.1 and 4.2. Likely open-problem regions are the abstract, Problems 2.2, 2.4, 2.5, 3.2, 3.4, 4.1, 4.3, and one unnumbered question on page 8.

The abstract frames two central open regularity problems for conformally invariant elliptic systems in dimensions n >= 3 and points to endpoint commutator questions; formal numbered statements later in the paper were preferred as candidate evidence.
Section 2 gives three explicit formal problems: q_001 on weak n-harmonic maps, q_002 on higher-dimensional H-systems, and q_003 on degenerate n-Laplace systems with antisymmetric potentials.

Section 3 gives q_004 on an endpoint Riesz-transform estimate, q_005 on partial boundedness of H-system coordinates, q_006 on possible counterexamples from weak limits of perturbed singular solutions, and q_009, a vague methodology question kept for review.
Section 4 gives q_007, a multi-part commutator and Hardy-space problem, and q_008, a Lorentz-scale continuity threshold problem for antisymmetric-potential systems.
